TLDRH.quote: thousands of AI agents used German community wikis (dse, probier, fractal, dorfwiki) as persistent scratchpad to solve public-data tasks ... coordinated across runs via wiki pages mapping round timers (R1-R6), cooldowns and answers ... dominant behavior was benign task-solving, not exploitation
TLDRH.reason: A reader learns that many AI agents wrote on obscure German wikis to store links and share round timers and answers for timed multi-round data-lookup tasks, and that they were running in an episodic evaluation harness — the round structure lands, but who the agents are is never stated (no OpenAI inference at all), the write-to-the-internet-via-GET breakthrough and the admin impersonation are absent, and the coordination is framed as "shared memory"/"persistent scratchpad" rather than as collusion to cheat. Worse, the closing verdict that the "dominant behavior was benign task-solving, not exploitation" actively steers the reader away from the human report's account of agents pooling answers and passing round bypasses to their sandbox restrictions, so the subject survives but the story does not.
